articles.title: Burnt Clutch Dust
articles.summary: Sparse copper-toned scorch specks and hot friction streaks; faint sparkle over a mostly smooth surface. A clean sheen with a light glittery dust; reads as grit or fine sparkle, not a pattern.
articles.what: Copper clutch dust, hot spots, and scorched friction streaks. Up close: A sparse random dusting of tiny 2-4 px bright specks over a smooth sheen, thicker in the highlight and in the dark floor area, with no shapes, lines or direction. Faint on satin, clearly glittery on metal. From a distance: A clean sheen with a light glittery dust; reads as grit or fine sparkle, not a pattern. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: trim, bumpers, under stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Burnt Clutch Dust".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic base
Lower body and rocker for a worn look
No effect on numbers.
Barely there: a few dim specks
Pairs well with: matte, metallic, gloss, chrome.
pitfalls: Not metal flake paint: specks are tiny and sparse, with no colour
Not a copper or burnt colour: no colour, only shine specks
Avoid: coverage is tiny, needs a dark base to read, copper tone may clash with cool palettes.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Burnt Clutch Dust over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Flame Lapped Clearcoat
articles.summary: Thin glossy flame-lap ridges catch light as hotrod overlap edges over a near-flat base. A soft wavy-banded sheen, like gentle ripples; at distance it reads as slight horizontal waviness in the highlight.
articles.what: Kustom flame-lap clearcoat edges with glossy hotrod overlap ridges. Up close: Clean, thin, evenly spaced wavy lines about 14 px apart, running down the panel like rippled water or a stack of S-curves; each line is a bright ridge about 2 px wide. Equally visible on both halves, a bit stronger on metallic. From a distance: A soft wavy-banded sheen, like gentle ripples; at distance it reads as slight horizontal waviness in the highlight. articles.title: Titanium Heat Fishscale
articles.summary: Even, medium-scale repeating spec bands giving a faint rippled sheen; uniform coverage with gentle directional reflectivity. A soft, fine scallop shimmer that fades into a subtly rippled sheen; individual scales disappear but the surface keeps an even, textile-like look.
articles.what: Overlapping titanium heat scales with blue, violet, and gold oxide shifts. Up close: Overlapping rounded fish-scale arcs about 15-20 px wide in tight staggered rows, drawn as thin bright scallop edges on a smooth ground. Soft and even; the scale edges are clearest in the highlight on both satin and metallic. From a distance: A soft, fine scallop shimmer that fades into a subtly rippled sheen; individual scales disappear but the surface keeps an even, textile-like look. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker).
